easy.def: A small bag sewn into clothes.
examples: I put it in my pocket.
My pants have two pockets.
Keep your hands in your pocket.

more.def: A small bag sewn into clothing for holding small things.
examples: She keeps a tissue in her pocket.
His coat has deep pockets.
I found a coin in my jeans pocket.

related.def: As much as a pocket can hold.

examples: The pencil has a point.
Do not touch the point.
The star has five points.

more.def: The sharp, thin end of something.
examples: The point of the needle is very sharp.
The pencil broke at the point.
A star has five points.
We got a point.
She scored a point.
The game is tied by a point.

more.def: A unit used to keep score in a game or contest.
examples: Our team scored three points before the break.
You get one point for every right answer.
She won the game by two points.

easy.def: To show where something is with your finger.
examples: I point at the bird.
She pointed to the door.
Point to the moon.

more.def: To show where something is by holding out a finger or an object toward it.
examples: The guide pointed to the top of the cliff.
She pointed at the map to show where we were.
The arrow points north.

easy.def: Something that can make you very sick.
examples: Poison is dangerous.
Some mushrooms are poison.
The bottle said poison.

more.def: A substance that can make a person or animal very sick or kill it.
examples: Some snakes have poison in their fangs.
The label warns that the cleaner is poison.
Some wild mushrooms are poison.

easy.def: People whose job is to keep a town safe.
examples: The police helped us.
Call the police.
A police car drove by.

more.def: A group of people whose job is to keep the public safe and to make sure laws are followed.
examples: The police helped the lost boy find his parents.
A police officer stopped the traffic so the children could cross.
The police station is next to the library.
The school has a policy.
The policy is no phones.
It is our policy.

more.def: A set of rules or plans that people agree to follow.
examples: The school has a policy about running in the halls.
The store has a return policy.
It is our policy to share.
It is polite to say "thank you."
The polite girl said "please."
Be polite to the bus driver.

more.def: Having good manners and showing respect for other people.
examples: The polite boy held the door open for everyone.
It is polite to wait until everyone is served before eating.
He wrote a polite letter to thank his aunt.

easy.def: Having to do with the government and how a country is run.
examples: Voting is a political act.
The mayor is a political leader.
We learned about political parties.

more.def: Having to do with government, leaders and the way a country or city is run.
examples: The class learned about political leaders in our country.
A political party chooses people to run in the election.
The mayor gave a political speech.

easy.def: Dirty things that hurt the air, water, or land.
examples: Smoke from cars makes pollution.
Pollution makes the air dirty.
We pick up trash to stop pollution.

more.def: Harmful or dirty things that spoil the air, water, or land.
examples: Pollution in the river made it unsafe for the fish.
Factories must work to cut down on pollution.
Noise pollution from the airport bothers the neighbors.

easy.def: A place filled with water for swimming.
examples: We swim in the pool.
The pool is cool.
Kids splash in the pool.

more.def: A large tank of water for swimming.
examples: We swam in the community pool.
The pool is deep at one end.
She learned to dive at the pool.
A pool of water.
Frogs sit by the pool.
There is a pool of rain.

more.def: A small area of water that has collected in one place.
examples: After the storm, a pool of water stayed on the road.
Frogs gathered by the shallow pool.
Starfish live in rock pools by the sea.
The poor family needed food.
They were poor, but happy.
The poor village had one school.

more.def: Having little money or few things.
examples: Long ago, a poor farmer found a magic bean.
Some poor families get help buying food.
The poor town had one old school.

easy.def: Used when you feel sorry for someone.
examples: Poor kitten, you are wet!
Poor baby is tired.
The poor bird hurt its wing.

more.def: Used to show that you feel sorry for someone.
examples: The poor puppy is shivering in the rain.
Poor Max had to stay home with a cold.
The poor kitten was stuck in the tree.
His writing is poor.
The poor light made it hard to read.
Poor weather ruined the picnic.

more.def: Of low quality or not good enough.
examples: The sound in the old theater was poor.
She got a poor grade because she did not study.
A poor harvest meant less food for the winter.

easy.def: To burst with a short sound.
examples: The balloon popped.
Corn pops in the pan.
Bubbles pop.

more.def: To burst or break open with a quick, short sound.
examples: The balloon popped and made me jump.
Popcorn kernels pop when they get hot.
I heard the soap bubbles pop.
I heard a pop.
The balloon went pop.
A pop came from the fire.

more.def: A short, sharp sound like a small burst.
examples: The cork came out with a loud pop.
We heard a pop from the fireplace.
The balloon burst with a pop.
Soccer is a popular game.
This is a popular book.
Pizza is popular with kids.

more.def: Liked or enjoyed by many people.
examples: That song is so popular that everyone knows the words.
The beach is popular with tourists in summer.
She is popular because she is friendly to everyone.

easy.def: The place or way something is.
examples: Stay in your position.
Put the ball in position.
I changed my sitting position.

more.def: The place where something is, or the way it is placed.
examples: The players ran to their positions on the field.
Sit in a comfortable position.
Check the position of the hands on the clock.
She has a new position.
He applied for a position at the zoo.
The school has a position open.

more.def: A job in a company or group.
examples: She applied for a position at the library.
He holds an important position at the bank.
The school has a position open for a cook.

related.def: To move something to a new position.

examples: She has a positive attitude.
Be positive.
He is positive.

more.def: Thinking about the good side of things.
examples: She has a positive attitude about school.
A positive person looks for the bright side.
He felt positive about the test.
I am positive.
He is positive he locked it.
She was positive about the answer.

more.def: Completely sure about something.
examples: I am positive that I locked the door.
He was positive about the answer.
She was positive the bus was late.
There is a possibility of rain.
A snow day is a possibility.
Winning is a possibility.

more.def: A thing that might happen or might be true.
examples: There is a possibility that the game will be canceled.
Scientists studied the possibility of life on other planets.
We talked about every possibility before choosing a name.
It is possible to fly.
Is it possible to go?
Rain is possible.

more.def: Able to happen, be done or be true.
examples: It is possible to see the stars from here on a clear night.
Is it possible to finish before lunch?
Snow is possible tomorrow, but it may rain instead.

easy.def: A tall piece of wood or metal in the ground.
examples: The fence post is tall.
A post holds the sign.
The horse is tied to the post.

more.def: A strong, upright piece of wood or metal set in the ground.
examples: Dad nailed the sign to a post.
The horse was tied to a fence post.
A tall post held up the porch roof.

easy.def: To put up a sign or message.
examples: Post the sign.
She posted a picture.
He posted a note.

more.def: To put up a notice or message where people can see it.
examples: The teacher posted the schedule on the door.
She posted a photo on the class page.
He posted a sign by the gate.
Post the letter.
I posted a card.
He posts letters.

more.def: To send something by mail.
examples: Mom posted the letter on the way to work.
I posted a card to my cousin.
He posts packages on Fridays.

easy.def: A deep round dish for cooking.
examples: Mom cooked soup in a big pot.
The pot is hot.
Put the pasta in the pot.

more.def: A deep, round container used for cooking or for holding plants.
examples: The soup simmered in a big pot on the stove.
She planted a seed in a small clay pot.
He stirred the pot of chili with a wooden spoon.

easy.def: A round vegetable that grows in the ground.
examples: I eat a baked potato.
Potatoes grow underground.
Mom mashed the potato.

more.def: A round vegetable with brown skin that grows under the ground.
examples: Dad baked a potato for dinner.
Potatoes grow underground, and farmers dig them up.
She made French fries from a potato.

easy.def: A way to measure how heavy something is.
examples: The baby weighs ten pounds.
I bought a pound of apples.
A pound of flour is heavy.

more.def: A unit for measuring weight, equal to 16 ounces.
examples: The baby weighed eight pounds.
We bought a pound of apples.
The bag of flour weighs five pounds.
Rain pounded on the roof.
He pounded the drum.
Waves pound the shore.

more.def: To hit something hard many times.
examples: Rain pounded on the roof all night.
He pounded the nail into the board.
Waves pound the shore during a storm.

easy.def: To make water flow out of something.
examples: Pour the milk into the cup.
I pour water on the plant.
She poured the juice.

more.def: To tip a container so that a liquid flows out.
examples: Dad poured the batter into the pan.
Rain began to pour down all at once.
He poured water from the pitcher into each glass.

easy.def: The strength to make things happen.
examples: The wave had great power.
I used all my power to push.
Superheroes have special powers.

more.def: The ability or strength to do something or to make something happen.
examples: A hurricane has enough power to knock down trees.
Whales have great power in their tails.
The king had the power to make new laws.
The storm cut the power to our street.
Solar panels make power from sunlight.
We lost power, so I used a flashlight.

more.def: Energy, especially electricity, that is used to run machines and light buildings.
examples: The power went out in the whole city during the storm.
Windmills turn wind into power for homes.
A small battery gives power to the toy car.
A powerful engine.
The wind was powerful.
He is a powerful swimmer.

more.def: Having great power or strength.
examples: The powerful engine lifted the rocket.
A powerful storm knocked down trees.
The king was a powerful ruler.
